t:
(a) 
Sections 1–5 of this Act restate, without substantive change, the laws replaced by those sections on the effective date of this Act. Laws effective after June 30, 1968, that are inconsistent with this Act supersede it to the extent of the inconsistency.
 
    (b) 
References made by other laws, regulations, and orders to the laws restated by this Act are deemed to refer to the corresponding provisions of this Act.
 
    (c) 
Actions taken under the laws restated by this Act are deemed to nave been taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.
 
    (d) 
Sections 1(2) and 1(14) of this Act are effective as of September 11, 1967, for all purposes.
 
    (e) 
Sections 1(13)(B) and 1(17) of this Act are effective as of September 6, 1966, for all purposes.

fable.w: This section is a technical restatement and effective-date provision for a codification act. The tempting reading is that the words "regulations" and "Actions taken" signal rulemaking or a challengeable federal decision, but they only cross-reference existing laws and deem past actions to fall under the restated provisions. No outside party is consulted, heard, given a seat on a body, or granted a right to sue, and no new rulemaking authority is conferred.
fable.s: References made by other laws, regulations, and orders to the laws restated by this Act are deemed to refer to the corresponding provisions of this Act.

opus.w: This section only says that references in existing laws, regulations and orders now point to the restated provisions, that past actions stay valid, and when certain sections take effect. Mentioning "regulations" here does not give anyone authority to make rules. Nothing in the section brings states, experts, the public or any other outside party into a federal decision, so it is not participation.
opus.s: References made by other laws, regulations, and orders to the laws restated by this Act are deemed to refer to the corresponding provisions of this Act.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The words "regulations, and orders" and "Actions taken" could look like rulemaking or agency decisions involving outsiders. That reading fails. This is standard codification boilerplate. It keeps old cross-references and past actions valid and sets effective dates. It gives no rulemaking authority and creates no consultation, hearing, advisory body or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard savings clause and technical provision regarding the restatement of existing laws and their effective dates. It does not establish any new advisory bodies, comment periods, consultations with outside entities, or rights to sue. It merely clarifies that the new text replaces the old text without substantive change, which is a legislative housekeeping matter, not a participation mechanism.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Sections 1–5 of this Act restate, without substantive change, the laws replaced by those sections on the effective date of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Act restates laws, it implicitly carries forward any participation mechanisms in those laws. However, the definition requires the *section itself* to recommend or require participation. This section is purely a savings clause and technical amendment provision regarding the effective dates and references of the restated laws. It does not create, mandate, or describe any process for outside parties to consult with the government.
